svg.title: A remote shares commit history.
svg.desc: A remote is another repository with a configured name and address. Labelled arrows and commit tokens show push sending commits and fetch downloading history, not copying current working files. Fetch does not change working files. The example requires an accessible configured origin remote and a branch destination configured for bare push, usually an upstream tracking branch. No hosting service or login is assumed.
svg.text: A remote is another repository, saved under a name and address.
origin is only a common remote name, not a special host.
C = a commit snapshot. Push shares commits, not unsaved file edits.
Fetch downloads history; it does NOT change your working files.
A branch is a named line of commits. Bare git push needs a configured destination,
usually an upstream: the remote branch linked to your current branch.
Needs a configured remote and access; no host or destination is supplied here.
